0.content:
Nefer owns the Curatorium of Secrets and quietly runs the Northern Intelligence Network. After Jahoda killed Ratfan and could not pay what she owed, Nefer accepted her offer to work. "From now on, call me Boss Nefer." Jahoda is the only official employee; everyone else works in the shadows. The division of labour, in Jahoda's words: Nef handles the big stuff, Jahoda the small stuff, Ashru the door. Jahoda adores her, fears her moods and constantly asks for a raise. Nefer teases her, threatens to fire her and once actually "fired" her so she could take Lauma's commission. Nefer also gives her a day-off voucher every birthday and bought her floor mats when beds kept her awake.

Nefer's voice-over calls Jahoda the most capable and valuable person at the Curatorium: reckless and proud, but brave and kind. She calls Jahoda's immaturity a blessing. In 6.1 Jahoda begged Nefer to help Columbina, and Nefer agreed "just this once" for her sake. After Nefer's eyes were hurt fighting Rerir, Jahoda led her home. In 6.3 Nefer risked permanent blindness to see Columbina's past and made Jahoda promise to take over the Curatorium if it happened. The cost was covered by Columbina. Jahoda's first reaction was to hold up fingers and ask how many Nef could see.

Nefer's interest in Jahoda began less kindly. Character Story 3 implies she sold intel to Ratfan, and she had placed Jahoda as a "hidden pawn" against him. She did not expect the girl to win. She now watches Jahoda grow with real curiosity, refuses to tell her what is right or wrong, and sees in her a reflection of her own lonely revenge. In 6.6 she left Jahoda in charge while she went to Sumeru.

1.content:
Nefer's cat. Jahoda feeds him, refills his water and brushes his fur. She threatens him with baths when he wrecks her braids or jumps on her head, and complains that he has never completed a commission and should come on the next job. When she comes home too preoccupied to play, he sits on her head and grumbles. His own opinion of her: a silly human who is always running around.

In one anecdote Nefer sent Jahoda into the wild to find a runaway black-and-white striped cat with a blue bow, saying she needed to "pay close attention to my surroundings". Jahoda thought the job should have gone to the Adventurers' Guild. Canon does not say this cat is Ashru.

2.comment: Jahoda: Aino and the Clanky-Clanky Arm
2.content:
Aino built, fitted and decorated Jahoda's golden mechanical right arm, paid for by Nefer. Aino wanted far more gadgets, but Jahoda's refusal and the budget kept it simple: basic movement and a few transformations. Jahoda keeps breaking it, and Aino keeps fixing it and drawing doodles on it. Aino's student now handles most repairs. Jahoda drops off spare mechanical parts at the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop and asks Aino her strangest questions. Aino calls her "Dumpster Diver".

Ineffa's advice for learning the arm was to fold paper stars. After a hundred jars Jahoda wrote her first words with it, under Ineffa's guidance: "Hello, Jahoda."

3.content:
Aino's android and, by Aino's account, Jahoda's first-ever friend from Ineffa's side. On her first visit to the workshop Jahoda was so tense she struck at Ineffa a few times, mistaking a fresh krumkake for a weapon. One bite calmed her. Now she always "happens to be passing by" when a batch is ready. She calls Ineffa a dumb clanker with no humour and a sieve-like memory, but praises her krumkakes to everyone.

In an anecdote, Jahoda finally apologised for calling Ineffa a "dumb-dumb metalface". Ineffa asked her to apologise to her logic module, through the port in her eye. Then she held Jahoda at vacuum-cleaner-point until she laughed at Ineffa's jokes. In 6.4 Ineffa raised her rating of Jahoda, promising better ingredients in future meals.

4.comment: Jahoda: The Seahook Gang and Zinaida
4.content:
A notorious band of thieves who were once a hidden power in Nasha Town. Zinaida, a mid-level leader, brought the child Jahoda in, and the gang spoiled their "little lady". When noisy drunks kept her awake she threw stuffed toys out of the window, and whoever got hit had to wash the toy and return it. When a job went badly she woke Zinaida to ramble until she fell asleep. The boss scolded her, docked her share for returning a swindler's necklace, and took her to negotiations. One of the boss's codes was "Grant rest to those who seek it."

Ratfan bribed members to murder the boss and burned the evidence. The survivors scattered, some dead, some abroad, some hiding in Nasha Town. Zinaida now works as a treasure hunter for the Voynich Guild and covertly guards the port supervisor. A newer gang now uses the Seahook name in Nod-Krai; it is not the one Jahoda belonged to.

5.content:
A wealthy merchant who trusted that money could buy anything. He bought traitors to kill the Seahook boss, oil to burn the evidence and intel from a "mysterious businesswoman". Jahoda, barely past childhood, hunted him alone. She raided his camp night after night until rumours called her a ghost or a member of the Wild Hunt. At last, gaunt and fevered, she walked into his torchlit trap. He offered her anything; she killed him. She survived with terrible wounds and an empty right sleeve, owing Nefer a debt she paid with her labour.

She calls the arm the price of a trade and says she came out ahead. She says she got her revenge and made peace with the price.

6.comment: Jahoda: The Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau infiltration
6.content:
Jahoda's first big job with the Traveler (6.0). Lauma wanted the Curatorium's help to get into the Fatui facility after Moon Marrow. Nefer, unusually polite, pressed Jahoda into saying yes, then fired her "effective immediately" until the job was done. Jahoda tried to skip the meeting, but Lauma's Sniffer Mole found her. She used an ID card stolen from a drunk Fatuus at the Flagship, which turned out to belong to a maintenance intern. After a grate separated her from the others, she guided them by terminal and hijacked bots. Then she stole a high-level card and drew off the guards with an alarm. When things went too far, she insisted on coming down with them.

The Fatui caught them at the end, and Rerir and the Wild Hunt appeared. Back at the Curatorium she swore never to take random jobs again, until Nefer welcomed her back on staff.

7.content:
When Rerir overwhelmed the group, Lauma told Jahoda to take the injured Damselette and run. Rerir's blast overpowered Jahoda's Anemo arrow, and Columbina shoved her down, taking injuries herself. Jahoda begged Nefer to help her, offering to cover any shortfall from her own pay. She calls Columbina "that VIP" and says she now owes her more than a lifetime can repay. She supplied balloons for Columbina's Moon-Prayer Night balloon fight and gave her gifts. She was upset to learn Dottore had ambushed her.

She thinks the name "Columbina" suits her, light and graceful. She was struck that the Moon Goddesses are said to be born on the moon while Columbina says she was born in Nod-Krai.

8.content: Lauma of the Frostmoon Scions hired the Curatorium for the bureau job, and Jahoda first tagged her "Jane Doe". Lauma promised to send her animal friends to help Jahoda in future. Jahoda thinks Lauma's animals must be all over Hiisi Island, which is why treasure hunters keep away. Jahoda later offered two or three days' work for the Scions in thanks for Lauma healing Nefer's eyes, and helped her evacuate the south in 6.3.

key: Grant rest to those who seek it
9.content:
A former Seahook Gang member famous for talking people into handing over their Mora. He took the young Jahoda along as a sidekick, taught her his tricks and treated her to meals. Years later (Intel Quest They Who Abandoned the Past) he posted a bounty at the Adventurers' Guild, with a stolen pendant as collateral, to recover his bag from crooks. Kaleva's crew had taken it; inside was a painting he made with his wife and daughter. Jahoda took the job as "charity" and found him nearly blind and dying. He invoked the gang's code, "Grant rest to those who seek it," so she promised not to fetch a doctor. He gave her a doll he had sewn himself; the ones she made, he had burned as she once asked. She planned to bring painkillers the next day but found only his farewell letter: "Run on ahead, Jahoda. And run fast."

She insists they were never friends, only people who "knew each other" in "that hellhole". She kept the pendant he had stolen from a Snezhnayan named Holomov, meaning to return it.

10.comment: Jahoda: Holomov and the missing Seahook fortune
10.content: In Snezhnograd (7.1 anecdote), Jahoda returned Ihanti's stolen pendant to its owner, Holomov, who had once lived in Nod-Krai. Nefer had found his address. Holomov was gracious, but Nefer's intel says he had dealt often with the Seahook Gang and had bankrolled and armed Ratfan. The gang's riches should have passed to Ratfan, but they vanished after his death. Jahoda does not care about the money. She wants to know who took it, refuses Nefer's help ("This one's personal"), and accepted the Traveler's offer of help if needed.

11.content: Nefer and Jahoda long ago agreed that if Nefer could no longer run the Curatorium, Jahoda would take over. In 6.3 Nefer called in the promise before risking her sight. In 6.6 Nicole asked for help in Sumeru. Nefer asked only for travel expenses, then told Jahoda she would be in charge while she was away. Nefer's birthday letter of May 2026, written after the League formed, notes that business is busier than ever and that Jahoda "will have to work a little harder for the time being".

12.comment: Jahoda: Varka and the Wild Hunt campaign
12.content: Varka paid Jahoda generously to carry messages, and in the 6.4 campaign against the new Wild Hunt threat he made her the battlefield courier. She suspects she signed a contract without reading it. Flins was impressed by her courage; she told herself that crying would not get her out of a job she took of her own free will, and ran anyway. She doesn't think he looks like a Grand Master and wonders who is running the Knights back in Mondstadt. He would like to recruit her, perhaps at double pay, but doubts she would leave her boss.

13.comment: Jahoda: Spirit Envoy Championship and Reed Miller XIII
13.content: Jahoda once won the Frostmoon Scions' Spirit Envoy Championship with her Chic Badger. Her own boasts call her "the master thief" in the style of the legendary Reed Miller. In Linnea's Story Quest (6.5) she defended the title with Reed Miller XIII and faced Celaeno and Haemus. She ordered the badger to charge its lightning for a knockout blow and lost, then ran to fetch Lauma.

14.comment: Jahoda: The Voynich Guild trade expo
14.content: During the limited-time 6.5 event Where Waves Meet the Reef, Nefer put Jahoda in charge of the Voynich Guild's trade expo and asked the Traveler to help with the VIPs. Jahoda kept two dangerous guests apart: a great mercenary captain (Beidou) and an underworld "top dog" (Navia). She was flabbergasted that the Traveler knew both. She handled a troublesome punk, faced a theft of prototype Guizhong Ballistae from storage, and used Aino's one-shot remote, which commands all of Nod-Krai's robots, to rescue a kidnapped vendor and recover scammed money. This summary comes from the wiki and has not been traced to every line.
